clauses.text: (a) All habitable rooms in non-air-conditioned residential, business and mercantile buildings, apart from kitchen, store room, utility room, box room and garage, shall have a ceiling height not less than 2.75 m measured from the finished surface of the floor to the underside of the finished ceiling, or false ceiling. A maximum of one-third of the floor area of such habitable rooms may, however, have a minimum ceiling height of 2.44 m. For air-conditioned rooms in such buildings, the minimum ceiling height shall be 2.44 m. In the case of pitched roof without a horizontal ceiling the lowest point of the finished ceiling shall be at least 2 m above the finished surface of the floor and the average height of the ceiling shall not be less than 2.44 m.
clauses.notes:
Habitable room - a room used for living, sleeping, eating or working, as distinct from a kitchen, store, utility, box room or garage, which this clause excludes.

Ceiling height - measured from the finished floor surface to the underside of the finished ceiling (or false ceiling where one exists), not to the soffit of the slab above.

The 2.44 m concession applies to at most one third of a habitable room's floor area, and separately to the whole of an air-conditioned room.

clauses.text: (b) The minimum clear head room under the ceiling, folded plate, shell etc. and under the false ceiling or duct in an air-conditioned room shall not be less than 2.44 m. The minimum clear distance between the floor below and the soffit of a beam shall not be less than 2.15 m.
clauses.notes:
Clear head room - the unobstructed vertical distance to the lowest projecting element, which may be a duct, a folded plate or a down-stand beam rather than the ceiling plane itself.

Soffit of a beam - the underside of a beam projecting below the ceiling.

clauses.text: (c) The requirements of ceiling height for buildings of occupancy other than residential and business and mercantile shall be as given in Table 3.1.9.
clauses.notes: Occupancy classification decides which minimum applies. Table 3.1.9 raises the minimum for educational, institutional, health care and assembly buildings, and raises it further for industrial, storage and hazardous ones.
